Nidhi Gupta, J.

Present appeal has been filed by the claimants seeking enhancement of compensation of Rs.4,90,000 Rs.4,90,000/- awarded by the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Panchkula (hereinafter referred to as "the Tribunal"), vide Award dated 26.05.2023 passed in MACP/40/2020 dated 05.03.2020 filed under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act (hereinafter referred to as "the Act").

The 4 claimants are the husband and 3 sons aged 48, 45 and 30 years of the deceased Jagir Kaur (wife of claimant No.1 and mother of claimants No.2 No. to 4).
2. Brief facts of the case are that the ld. Tribunal on the basis of pleadings and oral oral &
documentary evidence adduced before it concluded that the deceased Jagir Kaur had died due to the injuries suffered by her in a motor vehicular accident that took place on 07.02.2020 1 of 5 Neutral Citation No:=2025:PHHC:057108 due to the rash and negligent driving of truck bearing registration No.HP-- 12C-8713 (hereinafter referred to as "the offending vehicle") by respondent No.1.
The offending vehicle was owned by respondent No.2 and insured by respondent No.3.
The above-said above said compensation was granted along with interest @ 6% % per annum.

3. Learned counsel for the appellant appellants seeks enhancement of compensation stating that the appellant appellants had filed claim petition claiming compensation of Rs.70 lakh on account of death of Jagir Kaur aged 62 years on 07.02.2020; whereas the learned Tribunal has aw awarded Ruldu Ram And Others vs Pala Ram And Others on 1 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/90182827/

7. Record reveals that age of the deceased was proven to be 62 years on the basis of her Aadhaar Card (Ex.R1) (Ex.R1).

The learned Tribunal has assessed the notional notion income of the deceased after considering the existing case law on the issue in great detail detail; including judgments of this Court in FAO-1016-2014 FAO 2014 titled as "Nar Singh & Others Vs. ICICI Lombard Insurance Co.

9. It may be pointed out that even no deduction has been made by the learned Tribunal towards personal expenses of the deceased.
The claimants No.2 to 4 are the 48, 45 and 30 year year-old sons of the deceased Jagir Kaur.

I find the 4 of 5 Neutral Citation No:=2025:PHHC:057108 compensation awarded to the appellants appellant to be more than just and fair in the facts and circumstances of the case.

No doubt Chapter Chapter-12 of the Act is a beneficial legislation yet, as cautioned by the Hon'ble Supreme Court, the same cannot be allowed to be treated as a windfall or a source of 'State of Haryana & Another Vs. Jasbir profit.
